title: Weekly Chief Inspector Report
contractor: West Tech Energy — Jose Salaises, Director of Operations

sections.heading: Executive Summary
paragraphs: This was a short week, with work Monday through a half day Wednesday ahead of the Thanksgiving break. West Tech finished welding out the 8" flare header, 8"-FL-12100-151S: all 55 welds on six isometric sheets. NDE is scheduled for Monday 11/30 to x-ray all of them. On the civil side, the pipe support rebar cages were tied, and we received the flare anchor details: two 7/8" F1554 Gr 36 anchors per leg with a shear hairpin, which means drilling the existing flare base plate holes out to 15/16".

The big change this week is the fuel gas tie-in. Operations will not allow a shutdown of the existing combustor, so the fuel gas piping is being rerouted through the rack. I met with the team on the routing on 11/24 and walked it down with West Tech. Six fuel gas isometric sheets are red-lined "do not fabricate" until Tegre issues revised ISOs, BOM and P&IDs; this is logged as potential change order PCO-01. Joel confirmed the schedule: piping and structural foundations / pipe supports complete by 12/18; platforms, I&E completion and commissioning in January. West Tech's tentative target is to finish NDE, hydrotest, rebar and all civil concrete pours by 12/5.

Decisions and items I need from MPLX / engineering: the updated flare anchor detail drawing, hold markup DWG. 2, the revised fuel gas ISOs, written direction on 100% RT (the ISOs still show 20%), and confirmation of the authorized tie-ins (SOW Rev 3 lists five in one section and four in another).

sections.heading: Safety & H₂S Summary
bullets: No incidents, near misses or H₂S alarms were reported this week.
No daily safety observations were recorded in my sources this week. Excavation, hot work and H₂S controls remain in effect per MPLX SOW Rev 3 (SAF-STD-0005, -0007, -0017).
Open: on-site safety coverage, fit testing for work under air, and air trailer inspection (action 9).
